column3: “Made” is rendered “built.”
“Not to carry … except the Levites” is rendered “No one is to carry … but the Levites.”

NASB adds “together.”
“Leader” is rendered “chief.”

“Chiefs of the fathers” is rendered “heads of the fathers' households”; NASB supplies “the place.”
The opening “for because at the first not you” is short in Hebrew; NASB fills it out as “Because you did not carry it at the first.” “Burst out against us” is rendered “made an outburst on us.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Word order is changed; “with the poles on them” is rendered “with the poles thereon.”
“Instruments of song” is rendered “instruments of music”; the order of the two stringed instruments is reversed, and their exact identity is not certain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“The second in rank” is rendered “of the second rank.” The Hebrew has the name “Ben,” which NASB keeps.
NASB supplies “were appointed.”
NASB has “harps” where the Hebrew word elsewhere in this chapter is rendered “lyres,” and adds “tuned to”; the meaning of “alamoth” is uncertain.
“Harps” is rendered “lyres,” and “to act as overseers” as “to lead”; NASB adds “tuned to.” The meaning of “sheminith” is uncertain.
“In a lifting up” is rendered “in charge of the singing,” and “a teacher” as “skillful.” The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; it may mean carrying rather than singing.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Blowing a trumpet on trumpets” is rendered “blew the trumpets.”
“Leaders of the thousands” is rendered “captains over thousands.”
“It was because God helped” is rendered “it came about because God was helping … that they sacrificed”; “young bulls” is rendered “bulls.”
“Wrapped” is rendered “clothed”; “the leader the lifting up the singers” is rendered “the leader of the singing with the singers,” and the meaning of the phrase is uncertain.
“Ram's horn” is rendered “horn”; the order of the two stringed instruments is reversed.
“It was the ark … was coming” is rendered “it happened when the ark … came”; “looked down through” is rendered “looked out of,” and “dancing” as “leaping.”
